pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert — Service: private-vpc-controlplane — Severity: P1
pagerduty-bot: Trigger: VPC connectivity checks failing for customer 'acme-corp' (us-west-2), 90% agent heartbeat loss.
incident-bot: Incident INC-1958765432 created and paged oncall-sre. Links: https://pd.example/incidents/1958765432
alyssa: Acked. I'm on-call. Pulling control plane health and agent heartbeat counts now. ETA 2m.
devon: On me for network traces if needed, ping me @devon
alyssa: Quick checks:
```
# control plane status
curl -s https://private-controlplane.us-west-2.redwood/status | jq .
{"status":"degraded","agent_heartbeat_loss_pct":92}
# agent heartbeats (sample)
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=agent -o wide | wc -l
12
kubectl -n redwood logs agent-3 | tail -n 80
[WARN] heartbeat timeout to vpc-peer-12
```
alyssa: Seeing a pattern: control plane reports degraded, most agent errors are TLS handshake failures to the customer VPC peer. Could be routing or ACL change.
mike: I can confirm BGP flaps from our edge to the customer's transit in the last 8 minutes. If their route withdrawn, TLS sessions drop.
sarah: Reached out to acme-corp network team (account manager looped). Asking if they pushed any firewall/routing changes. Email thread started.
devon: Can we test a traceroute from an onprem agent pod to the customer peer? Command:
```
kubectl exec -n redwood agent-3 -- traceroute 10.4.1.1
traceroute to 10.4.1.1 (10.4.1.1), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1 10.0.0.1 0.5 ms
 2 10.255.0.1 1.2 ms
 3 * * *
```
devon: Looks like path blackhole past our egress. I'm moving to escalate to network-oncall (pager).
incident-bot: Escalation: contacted network-oncall. PagerDuty incident linked.
alyssa: Customer impact assessment: Agents in us-west-2 for acme-corp are at ~92% offline for inference traffic. Control plane can accept API calls but private agents cannot reach customer VPC -> user impact: timeouts for private deployments; hosted unaffected.
mike: Workaround possibility: enable temporary egress proxy in us-west-2 to route via alternate transit (requires config + 10-15m to push). If customer needs immediate mitigation, we can try.
sarah: AC: contacted acme-corp NOC via phone. They reported maintenance window but didn't expect to withdraw routes. They're investigating.
alyssa: I'm going to open an incident ticket in Jira and add the temporary egress task to runbook. Jira: https://jira.redwood/INC-1958765432
alyssa: Quick mitigation steps I'm doing now:
 - Add alert suppression for noisy agent-heartbeat alerts for this customer
 - Kick a controlled restart of 2 agent pods to force re-establish TLS sessions
 - Prepare egress proxy plan if customer confirms route changes
devon: Acked handoff: I'll take over for the next shift at 00:00 UTC. Please paste any live tcpdump or pcap I should look at.
alyssa: Copying tcpdump to /tmp/acme-pcap-1958765432.pcap and syncing to s3://redwood-incidents/1958765432/
alyssa: Handoff notes: control plane degraded -> agent TLS handshake failures -> likely upstream routing withdrawal. Customer NOC looped, network-oncall paged. Next steps for devon: confirm if customer restored routes; if not, implement egress proxy plan with mike.
devon: Ack. I have the runbook link and will continue monitoring. If customer confirms permanent routing change, we'll schedule a follow-up to bake egress into the config and notify account.
incident-bot: Incident INC-1958765432 status updated to 'monitoring' by alyssa. Assigned: devon. Duration so far: 22m.
alyssa: Leaving the channel, ping if anything critical. :wave:
devon: Thanks, alyssa. I'll ping when I have next update or if we escalate to creating a K-incident.
oncall-sre: Monitoring continues. No further alerts in last 5m, but agent heartbeat still fluctuating between 8-14% online.
sarah: I'll keep customer comms updated. Logged customer impact: Private inference timeouts for affected nodes. Notifying CS.
